question: Which of the following is NOT a central bank’s function?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Banking facilities for the public**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Central banks primarily regulate and supervise the financial system, rather than providing direct banking facilities to the general public.
 
• Commercial banks are responsible for offering banking services such as savings accounts, personal loans, and other financial products to the public.
 
• Central banks focus on maintaining monetary stability, controlling inflation, and managing the nation's currency.
 
• They also act as a lender of last resort to commercial banks to ensure liquidity and stability in the financial system.
 
• Central banks provide financial services to the government and manage the country's foreign exchange and gold reserves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monetary Policy:**

 
 
• Central banks implement monetary policy to control inflation, manage employment levels, and stabilize the currency.
 
• They use tools like interest rates, open market operations, and reserve requirements to influence the economy.
 
 
 
• **Lender of Last Resort:**
 
 
• Central banks act as a lender of last resort to provide liquidity to commercial banks during financial crises.
 
• This helps prevent bank runs and ensures the stability of the financial system.
 
 
 
• **Currency Issuance:**
 
 
• Central banks have the exclusive authority to issue national currency and regulate its supply.
 
• This includes managing the design, production, and distribution of banknotes and coins.
 
 
 
• **Foreign Exchange Management:**
 
 
• Central banks manage the country's foreign exchange reserves and intervene in the forex market to stabilize the currency.
 
• They also facilitate international trade and maintain balance of payments stability.
